description_good_justification: The README opens with what Maré Player does: a COSMIC desktop application (panel applet or standalone window) for the TIDAL music streaming service. https://github.com/glima/mare-player
interact_justification: The README explains how to install and use it, and CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to report bugs, propose changes and contribute. https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md describes the contribution process: development setup, the checks a pull request must pass, commit message rules and how pull requests are merged.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#before-opening-a-pull-request lists the requirements: `just check` (clippy with denied lints, unused dependencies, licences, audit, i18n) and `just test-matrix` must pass, commits must be Conventional Commits, and new dependencies need a stated reason.
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers installation (COPR, building from source), first-time setup, usage, configuration and logs: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The user interface, its configuration and its MPRIS integration are described in the README's Usage and Configuration sections: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/README.md
sites_https_justification: The project site, repository and release downloads are all on GitHub over HTTPS; the Fedora packages are on COPR over HTTPS.
english_justification: Documentation and discussion are in English; bug reports and comments are accepted in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: 64 commits in the last 30 days, and dependency updates are merged regularly. https://github.com/glima/mare-player/commits/main
repo_track_justification: Git records every change, its author and its date.
repo_interim_justification: All work lands on the public main branch between releases; there are no private interim versions.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version and git tag (v0.3.6, ...): https://github.com/glima/mare-player/releases
version_tags_justification: Each release is a git tag (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH): https://github.com/glima/mare-player/tags
release_notes_justification: Every GitHub release carries human-readable release notes, generated by git-cliff from the Conventional Commits since the previous release and grouped by kind (features, fixes, security, ...): https://github.com/glima/mare-player/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No CVE has ever been assigned to mare-player. Security fixes, including dependency advisories, are committed with a security type and listed in the release notes' Security section.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported as GitHub issues; CONTRIBUTING.md says what to include: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs
report_responses_justification: Every bug report from others has been acknowledged, within six days at most: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/issues/1, https://github.com/glima/mare-player/issues/2, https://github.com/glima/mare-player/issues/3.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered, e.g. https://github.com/glima/mare-player/issues/41 was answered the day it was opened.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are public and searchable: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, as SECURITY.md explains: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported to the project. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 14 days.
build_justification: Cargo builds the project from source; `just build-release` builds and `just install` installs it.
build_floss_tools_justification: The Rust toolchain, Cargo, just and the GStreamer and libcosmic dependencies are all FLOSS.
test_justification: An automated test suite of unit and integration tests (around 880 tests) runs with `just test` / `cargo test`: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/tests
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` (or `just test`, `just test-matrix` for both feature sets).
test_most_justification: Codecov reports about 39% line coverage. Parsing, models, conversions, caching and state handling are tested; views and live TIDAL calls are exercised by hand.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the full test suite for both feature sets on every push to main and every pull request: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: new functionality comes with tests for whatever can be tested without a TIDAL account (parsing, models, conversions, helpers, state transitions); code that depends on the shape of TIDAL's responses is tested against fixtures trimmed from real responses. Views and live network calls are exercised by hand. https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent features and fixes came with tests, e.g. the playlist, favourites, followed-artists and mixes migrations, and the search category view. https://github.com/glima/mare-player/commits/main
tests_documented_added_justification: The test policy is in the pull request instructions: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests
warnings_justification: Clippy runs with `-D warnings`, and production code denies unwrap, expect, panic and unchecked indexing (`[lints.clippy]` in Cargo.toml).
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings fail `just check`, which CI gates on, so none are left in the tree.
warnings_strict_justification: Clippy runs with warnings as errors plus several restriction lints denied for production code.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design: least privilege (no listening ports, read-only CI tokens), HTTPS-only network access, secrets only in the system keyring, and fallible parsing of all external input. The model is documented in https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/SECURITY.md
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common vulnerability classes for this kind of software and how to avoid them: untrusted input is parsed fallibly, artwork URLs that are not HTTPS are refused, credentials are kept out of logs and error messages, and memory safety comes from Rust without unsafe code.
crypto_published_justification: Maré implements no cryptography. It uses TLS through rustls and OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, both published and reviewed protocols.
crypto_call_justification: All cryptography is delegated to dedicated libraries (rustls with aws-lc-rs for TLS); nothing is reimplemented.
crypto_keylength_justification: Key lengths are those of rustls' defaults, which meet NIST minimums; Maré generates no keys itself.
crypto_working_justification: rustls does not implement broken algorithms or modes.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: rustls does not offer algorithms or modes with known serious weaknesses.
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS through rustls uses ephemeral key exchange, so connections have perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Maré stores no passwords. It signs in with OAuth and keeps the resulting session in the desktop's Secret Service keyring.
crypto_random_justification: Session identifiers are UUIDv4 from the OS random source (getrandom), and the PKCE verifier comes from a cryptographically secure generator.
delivery_mitm_justification: Source and releases are delivered over HTTPS from GitHub; releases also ship SHA256SUMS and Sigstore-signed provenance (GitHub build provenance and SLSA level 3). https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-download
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are only published over HTTPS, next to signed provenance.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no unpatched publicly known vulnerabilities. Dependencies are checked by cargo audit in every CI run and by Dependabot, and advisories are fixed promptly (e.g. the rustls advisories of 2026-10-14 were fixed the same day).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical advisories are fixed as soon as they are known; see above.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository contains no private credentials. Only the public OAuth client id appears in the source; CONTRIBUTING.md forbids committing tokens, session dumps or client secrets.
static_analysis_justification: Clippy with warnings as errors on every build and in CI, and CodeQL on every push to main, every pull request and weekly: https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security queries for Rust look for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Confirmed findings are fixed in code rather than dismissed: CodeQL alerts 42 to 48 (false positives in test code) were resolved by changing the code, and real ones are fixed the same way. https://github.com/glima/mare-player/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_often_justification: Clippy runs on every build and in CI; CodeQL runs on every push to main, every pull request and weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A cargo-fuzz target (fuzz_lrc_parse, run with `just fuzz`) is run by hand from time to time, but not as a step before every release. https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/fuzz
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Maré is written in Rust and its own code contains no unsafe blocks.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests and fuzzing run debug builds, which enable Rust's debug assertions and integer-overflow checks; the fuzzer found an integer overflow in the LRC parser because of them. The code itself relies on types and fallible parsing rather than many hand-written assertions.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Issues found by fuzzing are fixed, e.g. an integer overflow in the LRC timestamp parser found by fuzz_lrc_parse, fixed with a regression test in https://github.com/glima/mare-player/blob/main/src/tidal/models.rs
